messages:
maria: quick heads-up: hit a nasty streaming edge in the python SDK while testing our onboarding sample. if the UI cancels mid-stream (user navigates away) the socket can remain open and we sometimes see duplicate final chunks when auth refresh kicks in.

sam: ouch. small repro? sounds like finalizer/aclose isn't firing and the retry path opens a new stream.

jess: boiled down repro below, using httpx chunked response:
```py
async def stream_text(resp):
    async for part in resp.aiter_text():
        yield part

# consumer stops early
async def consumer():
    async for chunk in stream_text(resp):
        if user_closed:
            return  # early return leaves socket open in our app
```
After return FD shows ESTABLISHED and stays until token refresh.

ben: confirmed. root cause is our public helper returning a custom object that implements `__anext__` but not the async generator protocol. Python's async-gen finalizer calls `aclose()` only for true async generators, so the underlying httpx response stays referenced and won't be closed. also we don't implement `aclose`/`athrow` on the wrapper.

maria: i also hit typing headaches: our stub types `AsyncIterable[str]` but callers expect `AsyncGenerator[str, None]` for explicit `aclose()` support; mypy flags it.

sam: that explains duplicate final-chunk: when an in-flight token refresh retries, code starts a new stream while old response still streaming; both push final boundaries into the app and it looks like dup output.

jess: minimal fix that worked in my local sample:
```py
async def _stream_gen(resp):
    try:
        async for b in resp.aiter_bytes():
            yield b.decode()
    finally:
        # always close underlying response regardless of how the consumer exits
        await resp.aclose()

# return the generator from the client API
return _stream_gen(response)
```
Also added `async def __aenter__`/`__aexit__` on the client helper so sample-app can do:
```py
async with client.stream_text(...) as it:
    async for line in it:
        ...
```
This made explicit lifetime management super clear for onboarding.

ben: for backwards compatibility i suggest: update stubs to `AsyncGenerator[str, None]` and add a type alias `AsyncIterableText = AsyncGenerator[str, None]` so existing users don't break. add a changelog callout.

sam: tests: unit test that returns early and asserts FD count normalizes; integration test that injects a 401 mid-stream and asserts we don't observe duplicate final-boundary semantics; add mypy run against stubs in CI.

maria: platform notes: uvloop on Linux triggers the fd-hang more frequently, windows sockets behave differently (TCP FIN timing), so adding CI variations helpful.

ben: also adding a `wrap_response_as_async_gen(resp)` helper so downstream sample apps and customers can reuse the correct pattern rather than rolling their own wrapper and getting it wrong. will include example in the sample-app README.

devex-bot: created issue #1967 "py-sdk streaming: ensure async-gen protocol support + safe early-cancel" and linked repro gist.

oliver: assigned to @ben and @jess. mark high priority for SDK stability/backwards-compat. add small note in migration doc for the type alias.

maria: small follow-ups: 1) ensure our httpx retry middleware cleans up previous responses before re-issuing streams, 2) consider emitting a debug metric when a response is closed by finalizer vs GC.

ben: ack. i'll prototype the generator-based wrapper, update stubs with alias, add tests and sample-app README snippet.

maria: thanks all, this should reduce onboarding friction + random flakiness for sample-app users.
